title: Real Madrid’s 10 Best Galacticos of All Time—Ranked
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Barnaby Lane3:00 PM ESTZidane and Beckham were both part of the original ‘Galácticos.’ / Boris Hovart/AFP/Getty ImagesFew clubs in world soccer have built their identity around superstardom quite like Real Madrid.

Long has the club built a reputation for acquiring the biggest stars in world soccer, assembling teams packed with extraordinary talent in pursuit of an unprecedented level of success. And the strategy has certainly worked. Real Madrid are not only the most successful club in Spanish soccer, but also the most decorated team in the history of European competition.

Over the years, countless superstars have walked through the doors of the Bernabéu, but a select few have come to represent something more than just expensive signings. They became Galácticos—the biggest names in the game, brought to Madrid with the expectation that they would deliver trophies, spectacular performances and a whole lot of headlines.

The concept was first aggressively pursued by Florentino Pérez during his initial presidency between 2000 and 2006, when the likes of Ronaldo Nazário and Zinedine Zidane arrived in Madrid. A second Galácticos era followed during Pérez’s return between 2009 and 2018, most notably associated with a certain Portuguese superstar whom we’ll refrain from naming just yet.

Now, Real Madrid find themselves in the midst of a third Galácticos era, once again headed by Pérez and his famously ambitious checkbook. It’s an era slightly more difficult to define given how commonplace enormous transfer fees have become across world soccer, but the landmark arrival of Kylian Mbappé—albeit on a free transfer—certainly fits the spirit of the policy.
But who are the greatest Galácticos of them all?

The word comes from galáctico, the Spanish term for “galactic”—something relating to a galaxy. In soccer terms, it describes a player whose talent, fame and stature are considered to be “out of this world.”

For our purposes, a Galáctico must be a genuine household name, arrive at Real Madrid for a major fee—or, in one case, huge wages to make up for it—and be signed during one of the three aforementioned eras.

That definition means several legendary Real Madrid players don’t make the cut. Raúl and Iker Casillas, for example, came through the academy, while Roberto Carlos arrived before the first Galácticos era, despite being widely regarded as one in his own right.

Fernando Hierro, Guti, Pepe, Marcelo, Casemiro, Dani Carvajal and Sergio Ramos are other notable omissions. Their impact on Real Madrid may have been greater than that of several players who do qualify, but they simply don’t fit the specific Galáctico criteria.
Claude Makélélé went under the radar at Madrid. / Andreas Rentz/Bongarts/Getty ImagesThere are a couple of names that deserve a special mention but don’t quite make the top 10.

First up is Claude Makélélé. Signed for a bargain €14 million from Celta Vigo in 2000, he was never the headline star in the way many of his teammates were. Instead, Makélélé provided the understated brilliance in midfield that allowed those bigger names to flourish. His supreme intelligence, positioning and tactical understanding made him an elite ball-winner and a vital piece of the puzzle, even if his reputation grew even more during his later spell at Chelsea.

From the second Galácticos era, Isco deserves a special shoutout. Because he was rarely the first name on the team sheet, the Spaniard never quite received the credit he deserved. But at his best, few could match him at the Bernabéu. A delightful midfielder with superb close control, intelligent passing and understated versatility, Isco won virtually everything with Los Blancos, including five Champions League titles.
Ask Real Madrid fans from that era who their favorite player was, and we’d bet our bottom dollar plenty of them would say Isco.

Beckham was one of the first Galácticos. / Phillippe Dezmazes/Getty ImagesGalácticos Era: FirstTransfer Fee: €37.5 millionFew, if any, players have ever fit the term “Galáctico” quite like David Beckham. He was one of the finest players in the world when he signed for Real Madrid in 2003, almost certainly the most famous footballer on the planet thanks to his celebrity status away from the pitch, and arrived from Manchester United for a then-hefty €37.5 million fee.As was the case with several Galácticos on this list, the major titles never quite came for Beckham in Madrid. His performances, however, still warrant his place here. He regularly wowed the Bernabéu crowd with his wand of a right foot, pinpoint crosses and trademark free kicks, while Real Madrid undoubtedly got plenty of bang for their buck when it came to his commercial appeal.During Beckham’s four years at the club between 2003 and 2007, his global profile helped generate an estimated $600 million in commercial and merchandising activity, making his arrival about far more than what he could produce on the pitch.

Kylian Mbappé is a striker who will define his generation. / Florencia Tan Jun/UEFA/Getty ImagesGalácticos Era: ThirdTransfer Fee: FreeKylian Mbappé is the landmark arrival of the third generation of Galácticos. Yes, he arrived for free—but his astronomical wages more than make up for the transfer fee Real Madrid would have had to pay Paris Saint-Germain.The Frenchman enjoyed a record-breaking debut season, scoring 44 goals—the most by any Real Madrid player in their first campaign with the club—before following it up with another 42 goals the following season.The goals have certainly arrived. Now, it’s up to the rest of his supporting cast to catch up. If they do, a glut of trophies should follow, positioning Mbappé nicely for a potential Ballon d’Or win.

Kroos is a Madrid icon. / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press/Getty ImagesGalácticos Era: SecondTransfer Fee: €25 millionIn some ways, Toni Kroos doesn’t quite fit the traditional Galáctico definition. He was hardly the flashy, larger-than-life personality typically associated with the label, and his relatively modest transfer fee from Bayern Munich hardly screamed “superstar signing.”But when Kroos arrived during Real Madrid’s second Galácticos era, he was arguably the finest midfielder on the planet, fresh off winning the 2014 World Cup with Germany.And his performances in a Madrid shirt were certainly “out of this world.”A master passer from deep, set-piece specialist and, on occasion, superb long-range shooter, Kroos became integral to an unprecedented era of domestic and European success at the Bernabéu. Alongside Luka Modrić and Casemiro, he formed one of the greatest midfield trios in soccer history.

Gareth Bale had a habit of clutch moments. /  Angel Martinez/Real Madrid/Getty ImagesGalácticos Era: SecondTransfer Fee: €100 millionFew, if any, players in Real Madrid history have had a knack for being as clutch as Gareth Bale.Five Champions League titles, three goals in finals—including arguably the greatest goal in the competition’s history, courtesy of a stunning overhead kick against Liverpool in the 2018 final.Then there was the 2014 Copa del Rey final. With the game level late on, Bale famously ran off the pitch—and off the field entirely—burning past Barcelona defender Marc Bartra with staggering pace before slotting home the winning solo goal in the 85th minute.Madrid’s fans may not have always loved him, and his famous fondness for golf certainly didn’t help matters. But when the biggest moments arrived, Bale had an uncanny habit of answering the call.

Luís Figo won the 2000 Ballon d’Or. / Mike Hewitt /Allsport/Getty ImagesGalácticos Era: FirstTransfer Fee: €60 millionA world-record transfer fee in 2000—infamously paid to Barcelona—made Luis Figo the first true Galáctico, and he set the standard incredibly high for those who would follow.A Ballon d’Or winner in the season of his arrival, Figo quickly set the Bernabéu alight with his dazzling feet, classy playmaking from the right wing and knack for finding the net himself. His goal against former club Barcelona in El Clásico in November 2001 only further endeared him to the Madrid faithful—and made him even more reviled by Barça supporters.Figo wasn’t simply the first Galáctico. He was the blueprint.

Luka Modrić won it all with Madrid. / Denis Doyle/Getty ImagesGalácticos Era: SecondTransfer Fee: €32 millionLuka Modrić might have reached the pinnacle of his individual career when he won the Ballon d’Or in 2018, but Madridistas were singing his praises long before—and long after—he claimed the prestigious award.One of only five players ever to win six Champions League titles, the diminutive Croatian brought a generational blend of class and quality to Real Madrid’s midfield. His ability to evade tackles, keep the ball under control under pressure and fire pinpoint passes through the eye of a needle made him one of the most complete midfielders of his generation.Modrić didn’t simply dictate the tempo. He controlled games, finding space where there seemingly wasn’t any and turning the most congested areas of the pitch into his personal playground.
